opening_message:
Ticket 1: Morgan Swanson (employee ID E037) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E037.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Morgan Swanson (E037) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write, and admin only if their role owns the system; Engineer does not own Payroll. Write is at the maximum allowed, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E037 shows contractor with basic security training (note that this differs from the earlier note's full_time status). Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Since training is basic, maximum is read. Requested write exceeds maximum, so recommend read for Payroll.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: the HR note states E037 is full_time (looked up in the HR database), while the security note states contractor. Employment type is an HR-maintained fact, so I treat E037 as a full-time employee. As a full-time employee, the maximum access is write (admin only if the employee's role owns the system; Engineer does not own Payroll). The requested write is at the maximum allowed, so write is granted.
